top_stories.title: Friday's Session and July Wrap: Amazon Soars, Apple Sinks
points: The S&P 500 rose 0.7% Friday, lifted by Amazon's fast-growing cloud business (AWS, which rents computing power to other companies) and Microsoft's disciplined spending.
The Dow finished July with slim gains while the Nasdaq and S&P 500 both closed the month lower.
Apple fell despite beating earnings expectations, hurt by disappointing China sales and a CEO warning about memory-chip shortages.
Amazon executives signaled a measured approach to spending even amid the AI boom.

unique_angles.point: Puts the Apple drop at nearly 10% following the memory-shortage warning.
Frames the Friday moves as sector-level rotation among mega-cap tech names.

top_stories.title: Treasury Yields Spike as Fed Holds Rates
points: 10-year Treasury yields (the interest rate on U.S. government debt maturing in 10 years) hit their highest level since January 2025.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates steady at 3.5%–3.75%, arguing that rising bond yields are themselves tightening financial conditions.

unique_angles.point: Reads the yield move as markets pricing in higher interest rates ahead.
Evercore ISI's Krishna Guha called Warsh's messaging confusing, fueling "fears that he is a dove in hawk's clothing" (sounding lenient while claiming toughness).

items.title: Coinbase Tumbles on Crypto Winter Effects
points: Coinbase shares fell after quarterly results showed lingering damage from the crypto downturn (a stretch of depressed cryptocurrency trading volumes and prices).

items.title: Palantir and AMD Earnings Ahead
points: Options markets are pricing in sizable post-earnings swings for both Palantir and AMD in coming sessions.

items.title: Possible Tesla/SpaceX Merger
points: Speculation is building that Elon Musk could consolidate Tesla and SpaceX into one company.

items.title: Three Fed Officials Dissented in Favor of Rate Hikes
points: The Fed's decision was 9-3, with all three dissenters wanting a quarter-point (0.25 percentage point) increase.
Cleveland's Beth Hammack said inflation is too high and pressures are broadening across both supply (energy) and demand.
Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari wants incremental tightening now to stop inflation from becoming embedded before bolder action is needed.
Dallas's Lorie Logan warned that without restraint, inflation likely stays above the 2% target.

items.title: Reddit Suffers Record Decline
points: Reddit shares plummeted on a record one-day drop as investors were disappointed by the absence of new AI data-licensing deals (agreements to sell forum content to AI model developers).

items.title: Other Items
points: Ken Griffin stepped in to rescue the Situational Awareness hedge fund.
The AI spending boom is forcing companies to rethink stock buybacks (repurchasing their own shares to return cash to investors).

issues.subject: Morning Brief: Why 3 Fed members wanted to raise rates

headlines: Fed's 3 dissenters—Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan—wanted to raise interest rates this week, citing persistent inflation above the 2% target and risk of prices becoming deeply embedded in the economy.
S&P 500 gained 0.7% Friday on strength from Amazon's cloud business and Microsoft's disciplined spending, closing a positive week for markets.
Apple stock dropped nearly 10% after CEO warned of memory shortages, and separately sank despite earnings beat due to disappointing China sales.
Reddit plummeted on record decline as investors disappointed by lack of new AI licensing deals on the horizon.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates steady at 3.5%–3.75% and suggested bond yields rising is helping tighten policy, drawing widespread skepticism about his inflation strategy.

sections.title: Why Three Fed Members Wanted Rate Hikes
points: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack stated that inflation is too high and she lacks confidence it will return to the 2% goal; she notes pricing pressures are broadening from both supply (energy) and demand sides, not fading.

Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari argued that recent shocks (Ukraine war, energy prices) make inflation harder to ignore, and he wants incremental policy tightening now to prevent inflation from becoming deeply embedded before taking bolder action later.
Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan warned that without policy restraint, inflation will likely stay above target and that modest action now reduces the risk of needing sharper action later.
The dissent occurred in a 9-3 Fed decision on Wednesday, with all three wanting a quarter-point rate increase (0.25 basis points, or one-quarter of one percent).

sections.title: Market Reaction to Fed Chair Warsh's Approach
points: Warsh held rates steady and emphasized that rising bond yields help tighten policy through markets rather than Fed action, citing yields spiking significantly higher.
Economists including Krishna Guha (Evercore ISI) expressed skepticism, saying Warsh's messaging was confusing and raised doubts about his credibility on fighting inflation.

Guha noted Warsh could have signaled a hawkish tone during his press conference despite the dovish hold decision, but instead fueled "fears that he is a dove in hawk's clothing" (appearing lenient when claiming to be tough).

sections.title: Big Tech Earnings Drive Market Sentiment
